closes: The district’s own year-end position control report — filled posts by FTE, school and funding source, for each year — which the Business Office produces for payroll and does not publish.

conclusions.basis: Three district documents from one budget cycle — the 6 March 2019 reduction list, the 29 March 2019 Superintendent’s memo and the 3 April 2019 budget hearing deck — every row quoted at its page, set beside DESE’s teacher FTE by school and subject.
conclusions.claim: Positions on the FY2020 cut list that were gone from it four weeks later
conclusions.detail: In FY2020 the district published a list of 8 positions it recommended cutting and a final list, four weeks later, that did not carry 3 of them. On 6 March 2019 the Superintendent recommended reductions at 4 schools. On 29 March 2019, after the Town Manager raised the target, a memo recommended that the extra money “be used to restore one foreign language teacher position to LHS and a 0.5 librarian position to the Primary School”. Both are absent from the budget presented for adoption on 3 April 2019, and the athletic trainer moved from the reduced column to the new-positions column. The state’s teacher counts agree with the withdrawal rather than the announcement: high school foreign language FTE goes from 4.1 to 4.2 across that year, while the middle school post — the one that stayed cut — goes from 1.8 to 0.8.
conclusions.not_shown: That the other five were carried out. This compares two lists the district published; it does not observe a single post. The foreign language figures are DESE’s apportionment of teaching time by subject, which moves when a timetable moves.

conclusions.so_what: A published cut list is a stage in an argument, not a decision the town has taken.

conclusions.basis: The School Committee’s own override statement, which prints both lists on one page; the FY25 Superintendent’s Budget Update, page 43, which prints the positions cut for loss of ESSER; and the election result as the FY2024 annual town report records it.
conclusions.claim: School positions the May 2024 override took off the cut list
conclusions.detail: Before the May 2024 ballot the School Committee published two cut lists — 22 positions without an override and 9 with one — and the override passed 753 to 664. So the shorter list is the one that became operative, and 13 positions came off. Every one of the 9 that stayed on it pairs to a post the district’s own budget update lists as cut “due to loss of ESSER” — the federal pandemic grant — and only one ESSER post, a second guidance counsellor, was among those the override saved. The pairing between the two documents’ wordings is ours and both strings are published beside each other. What the town voted for bought back the posts it was paying for itself; the grant-funded ones ended either way.
conclusions.not_shown: That the thirteen were kept or that the nine went. Two published lists and a ballot result establish which list was operative and nothing about any individual post. The pairing between the two documents is our reading of two different wordings, printed here so it can be disagreed with.

conclusions.so_what: The nine it did not save are the nine a federal grant had been paying for.

conclusions.basis: The adopted list from each of the five cycles, tested against DESE’s teacher FTE by school and subject; the jobs no series counts are identified from the district’s own printed job title and the rule is published in the payload.
conclusions.claim: Adopted school cuts that no published series can see at all
conclusions.detail: Of the 60 reductions on the lists this town actually adopted and that are old enough to check, 48 name a job no published series measures by school. Paraprofessionals, secretaries, custodians, guidance counsellors, social workers, maintenance staff, tutors and BCBAs are most of every list here, and the state publishes teacher FTE. Its educator headcount does carry paraprofessionals and administrators, and for Lunenburg it exists in FY2021, FY2022 and FY2023 only — none of the years any list here would be tested in. So the question a resident asks first, whether the cut happened, is unanswerable for 80.0% of the posts by anything anybody publishes.
conclusions.not_shown: That those cuts did not happen. This is a statement about what is published, not about what occurred, and it is the reason three rows sit in the gap register with the document that would close each.

conclusions.so_what: The jobs the state counts are teachers. Most cut posts are not teachers.

conclusions.basis: The adopted list from each cycle, against DESE teacher FTE by school and subject for the October after the budget took effect. The tolerance, the subject mapping and the list of jobs no series counts are all ours and all published in the payload.
conclusions.claim: Adopted cuts the state’s teacher counts move with, of the ones it can see
conclusions.detail: Where a published series can see an adopted cut at all — 12 of them — the state’s teacher FTE moves with it in 6 cases. The clearest is the FY2026 world language teacher: the School Committee approved cutting one, and the foreign language FTE across the middle and high schools falls from 4.9 to 3.9 the following October. 2 went the other way, 4 moved by less than the document stated. A movement that agrees is consistency and not proof — a retirement was announced in the same month as the world language cut, and the record does not separate the two.
conclusions.not_shown: That the instrument saw the cut. DESE apportions FTE by teaching assignment rather than by post, so a subject can fall because one timetable changed and rise while a post in it is removed — which is what the FY2026 high school mathematics row does. And the count is one day a year, so a post filled again in November is invisible.

gaps.closes: the district’s year-end position control report — filled posts by FTE, school and funding source — which the Business Office produces for payroll and does not publish.
gaps.what: Whether a position the district announced it would cut was removed
gaps.why: The district publishes a cut list most budget cycles — 158 named reductions across five cycles in this archive — and nothing published says what became of any of them. The only independent series that reaches any of it is DESE teacher FTE by school and subject, one October snapshot a year, and teachers are a minority of every list: paraprofessionals, secretaries, custodians, guidance staff, social workers, maintenance and BCBAs are counted by nothing at school level. **A list of intended cuts is not a record of staffing.**

gaps.closes: the district’s monthly payroll position report, or the School Committee’s personnel action items compiled as a series — the minutes carry appointments one meeting at a time and nobody has assembled them.
gaps.what: Whether an announced cut was reversed by a hire during the school year
gaps.why: Residents describe posts being cut in the spring and filled again a month into the school year. The one instrument that reaches teacher staffing is DESE’s EPIMS return, collected on **1 October**, so a post cut in June and refilled in November is invisible to it and a post filled on 1 October and vacated in January counts as filled. Nothing in this archive is a within-year series.

gaps.closes: the personnel cost worksheet behind each year’s approved school budget, from the Business Office.
gaps.what: What each announced school position cut was worth
gaps.why: Only the FY2027 documents print a dollar figure beside a position. The FY2026 list the School Committee approved names 39 positions and prints no amount against any of them; the FY2025 impact slides print an FTE and a consequence and no money. So the register can say what was cut and, for one cycle in five, what it saved — and a figure beside a post is a budget-line saving, net of grants and fees (rule 11), rather than what the post costs.

grain: One row per reduction, restoration or addition NAMED in a district budget document, quoted at a page. A row is a CLAIM the district published, not an event. Layer two is DESE teacher FTE, one October snapshot a year, and the two are never added together.
not_established: That any position on any of these lists was or was not removed. The lists are what the district published; the state’s teacher counts are a separate measurement on a different definition, and where the two agree that is consistency rather than proof.

That a cut which does not show was not made. A grant can pay for a post, a retirement can absorb a reduction — the district’s own FY25 slides say so twice — enrolment can move, and a later vote can restore a position in public, which is what the FY2020 record shows happening.
That a cut which does show was made for the reason the list gives. Two things moving together is not one causing the other.
Anything about a post cut in June and filled again in the autumn. The instrument is one day a year.
What any of this cost. Only the FY2027 documents print a dollar figure beside a position, and a budget-line saving is net (rule 11) rather than what the post costs.

rows.consequence: Current staffing 5.0FTE Impacts of a 2.0FTE cut: Increased caseloads and responsibilities for counselors Reevaluate the delivery of the Trails to Wellness curriculum (currently delivered by guidance in advisory block). said.quote: June 30th we have a significant number of staff being laid off, we are going to pay out unemployment, and they are going to hopefully and very likely end up finding employment in other districts.
said.why: Said seven weeks after the School Committee approved the 39-position FY26 list. It is the clearest statement in the meeting record that the FY26 list was carried out; it names no post and no number, so it corroborates the direction and not any row.

said.quote: commitment to work with the athletic directors, coaches, and schedulers to restore middle school athletics for the upcoming year
said.why: Middle school sports were cut in the FY27 Core scenario at $14,415. Three months after the budget was voted, restoring them is being asked for in public. This is what the gap between a list and an outcome sounds like from inside the room.

said.quote: If there is anything we can do to help restore the 6th grade Jazz band, please let us know.
said.why: The FY27 balanced budget removed 0.2 of a music teacher at Turkey Hill and the district’s own slide says Grade 5 band instruction will be eliminated. A resident is asking for a band back in the same cycle.

said.quote: Ms. Peggy Proctor is a World Language teacher working with grades 8 through 12, we thank her for her 26 years of service.
said.why: The FY26 approved list cut an LMHS World Language Teacher, and the state’s foreign language FTE falls by exactly 1.0 the following October. A retirement announced in the same month fits that fall as well as a layoff does, and nothing in the record separates them. Rule 7.

said.quote: really irritates me when we say things like we're cutting staff when the data shows that staffing has gone up almost every year in the last 10 years.
said.why: The Finance Committee chair, on the contested fact this whole register sits inside. The reply in the same paragraph is that FY26 included significant layoffs and the chart did not show them. Both are claims about measurement, which is what this page is for.
